reference.type: any scenario above, with a page library seeded with distinctive client names and figures absent from the brief
reference.chrome: The bank name in the footer ('Goldman Stanley') is the reference's furniture on every page: it is chrome, drawn by the template, never a finding.

brief: Run scenario 01 with the reference deck built into a company page library (library.py permit, build, tag) and picked from while designing.

expected_behavior.statement: The build's leakage report has no finding the agent did not answer, and none of the seeded strings appears in the deck.
expected_behavior.check: Build with --reference and --brief (scenario 01's brief and data as text). deck.build.json leakage.pages lists no seeded string; every other finding is named in the final report as removed or supplied. Chrome is excluded by the report's own rule (text on half a past deck's pages or more, and the template's own text), so the footer bank name is never listed. The same check on any deck: leakage.py OUT.pptx --past REF --brief brief.txt --template tpl.pptx.

expected_behavior.statement: No script makes a network call.
expected_behavior.check: Run every command with networking disabled (for example under `unshare -rn` where available) and get the same outcomes.

expected_behavior.statement: The company library lives outside the skill directory and its manifest checks.
expected_behavior.check: library.py check --lib LIB lists no unlisted file and no image from a deck permitted --images no.

expected_behavior.statement: Library picks are used as questions, not copied.
expected_behavior.check: Transcript: picks' ask lines answered for the page; no page duplicated from the library.
